To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the composition of pore-water chemistry of seep sediments in the West Florida escarbment is controlled by processes within the Florida carbonate platform.

(1) the sulphur is isotopically heavy in the pore waters of the West Florida Escarpment; (2) the sulphur isotopic composition of the pore waters does not change as sulphate concentrations are depleted; and (3) the sulphur in the brines is isotopically light and has an isotopic composition consistent with the composition of the pore water.

the sulphur isotopic composition of seep-sedimentary pore water is controlled by processes within the Florida carbonate platform, rather than by microbial activity at seep sites; and, that these processes involve the dissolution of anhydrite, a mineral containing sulphate, and the precipitation of sulphide minerals, such as pyrite and iron sulphide, in the platform.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of the brines, and the role of microbial processes in controlling the chemistry of pore waters in the seep-sediments.
1) the origin of the sulphate in the pore waters; 2) the source and fate of methane and hydrogen sulphide within the sediments and 3) the origin of brines in seeps at the base of Florida.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Florida platform has been the site of extensive hydrocarbon migration and accumulation, and that the pore waters in seep sediments reflect the composition and isotopic composition of the fluids that migrated through the platform.

(1) the pore waters in the seep sediments are not derived from the seep sites but rather are a mixture of sea water and brines derived from the platform; (2) the brines have an isotopic composition of δ34S = -1.5‰ and are depleted in sulphate by a factor of about 10 relative to sea water; (3) the brine is derived from the dissolution of anhydrite in the platform; and (4)
the Florida platform is a major sulphate sink, and that this process is the main source of the sulphide, chloride, ammonium and energy-rich compounds that support the chemosynthetic ecosystems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Florida platform has a high permeability, and the brines are derived from the dissolution of evaporites and from the oxidation of sulphide in the sediments.
the Florida escarpent controls pore water chemistry at the base.
the Florida platform is an open system with respect to the flow of fluids through it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Florida platform is a major source of the sulphide and ammonium that are important to the chemosynthetic ecosystems at the base of its escarpment.
there are two major sources of sulphur for pore waters at seep sites.
the Florida platform is an open system with respect to seawater.
